## Input.svelte

### `interface Props`

- `value` :: The text. Bindable; works controlled and uncontrolled.
- `onValueChange` :: Called with the new text whenever it changes, including when it is cleared.
- `size` :: The control height. Text follows this unless `textSize` is set. @default 'lg'
- `textSize` :: The text scale, independent of the control height. Follows `size` when omitted.
- `textColor` :: The ink of the leading icon and the clear button; muted by default so the value reads first.
- `shape` :: The corner shape. @default 'modern'
- `variant` :: `outline` is a bordered field, `secondary` a tinted one without a border, `ghost` is bare until hovered or focused. @default 'outline'
- `invalid` :: Marks the input invalid (red border, `aria-invalid`). Inside a `Field` it follows the field's error unless set.
- `icon` :: An icon drawn at the start of the field.
- `leading` :: Content drawn at the start of the field, after the icon — a prefix such as a currency or protocol.
- `trailing` :: Content drawn at the end of the field, before the clear button — a unit, a shortcut hint, a spinner.
- `clearable` :: Shows a clear button while the input has text. Escape clears it too.
- `ref` :: The underlying `<input>` element. Bindable, for focusing from code.
- `disabled` :: Blocks pointer and keyboard input, and dims the frame.

## frame.ts

### `interface FrameOptions`

- `variant` :: The surface of the frame. `outline` is a bordered field, `secondary` a tinted one without a border, `ghost` bare until hovered or focused. Any other canon variant reads as `outline`: a text field has no brand or status fill — that is what `invalid` and the field's own error are for.
- `size` :: The control height, from the `h-*` ladder.
- `textSize` :: Text scale, independent of the frame height. Defaults to `text-md`.
- `content` :: Height follows the content (a text area) instead of the size's fixed height.
- `grow` :: At least the size's height, taller as content wraps (a token field).

### `function frameClasses`

The classes of a text-entry frame, shared by every input in the kit. The frame is a `.field`, so it draws the focus ring for whatever is focused inside it.

### `function focusFrame`

Pointer-down on the padding or a decoration of a frame focuses its control, as clicking a native field would. Clicks on interactive children are left alone.
